analogs.covers: Role: a tiny cleaner that rides big herbivores, picks off parasites and has a taste for wounds
Social life: a noisy colony with harems, preening and begging, that mimics every sound

headline: An oxpecker riding the sauropods, living in a noisy parakeet colony that copies every sound.

setting.label: Wherever the sauropods roam, plus fishing waters
setting.note: Nomadic. Roosts on sauropod companions (Amargasaurus, Apatosaurus, Argentinosaurus), which shelter its chicks, and fishes and scavenges nearby.

playsLike: You are a Tiny aerial fisher and scavenger (air cruise 900, sprint 1,300 for 200 s). You don't hunt players: only fish, carrion and critters, and you flee if aggressed while scavenging. You clean parasites from sauropods and ride them, and up to 4 of you may stay latched on a sauropod companion while it's being hunted. Your colony has resident males with harems, and you mimic every sound you hear. As a last resort you can 'sting' an attacker, which leaves it hungry, thirsty and itchy but kills you within 30 minutes.

why.text: Mutualism with sauropods: cleans their parasites and uses them as roosts for its chicks. Oxpeckers and cattle egrets ride big grazers the same way (official inspiration: cattle egret).
The 'Rhamph sting' latches on and drains the victim's condition, a nod to vampire bats (official inspiration) and to oxpeckers that peck at wounds.
'Naturally mimic all sounds that they hear'. Parakeets do the same (official inspiration).
Unlimited colonies of female groups with resident males, bonding by preening and begging each other for food.
Fishes from the air and bobs in the water, grebe-like (official inspiration).

notLike: Oxpeckers call alarms to warn their hosts; Rhamphorhynchus goes silent and flies away when a carnivore approaches a herd.
Parakeets eat seeds and fruit; Rhamphorhynchus lives on fish, carrion and critters.
